anatomy.intro: The numbered illustration explains probable Mammillaria mammillaris; it is a botanical guide, not a measured portrait.

parts.function: Each projecting green mound is part of the succulent, photosynthetic stem.
parts.label: Tubercle

parts.function: The cushion at a tubercle's tip bears its spine cluster.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: Shorter outward-spreading spines form a protective star around the areole.
parts.label: Radial spines

parts.function: The stronger spine projects beyond the radial spokes.
parts.label: Central spine

flowers.text: The species' tiny cream, pale green, or yellowish flowers can hide between tubercles. The red projection recorded on this plant is fruit, not a petal; it reflects an earlier flower even after that bloom has disappeared.

growth.note: Use flowers and spine details to refine the probable ID; size alone cannot settle it.

stages.text: The green body is organized into spirals of tubercles.
stages.title: Rounded juvenile

stages.text: Established stems become larger globes or short cylinders.
stages.title: Broadening body

stages.text: Small pale flowers can be followed by conspicuous red club-shaped fruits.
stages.title: Flower and fruit

habitat.text: Mammillaria mammillaris occurs in the southern Caribbean and northern South America, including northeastern Colombia and northern Venezuela. It belongs to seasonally dry tropical vegetation. This is the natural background of a probable identification: the collection plant was purchased without a species label, and its nursery origin does not establish a wild locality.

Exactly four large legible numbered markers 1, 2, 3, 4, each once, with fine leader lines ending clearly on the named structures. No title, words, border, watering symbols or calendar. No flowers, grafts, or roots. Numbers must remain readable at 350px. Generic anatomical specimen, not measurement evidence. A Mammillaria mammillaris cactus: one rounded short cylinder, green prominent conical tubercles arranged in spirals, white wool in the gaps near the crown, sparse straight tan/dark central spines and shorter pale radial spines. Exactly 1 points to a green conical tubercle, 2 to a small spine-bearing areole at its tip, 3 to short pale radial spines, 4 to one long straight dark central spine. No red fruit.

lookalikes.name: Probable Mammillaria rekoi
lookalikes.text: The rekoi candidate has finer, denser pale radial spines and conspicuous hooked central spines; this plant's larger exposed tubercles and pale flowers support a different ID.

mature.text: LLIFLE describes rounded to short-cylindrical stems about 8–20 cm across, solitary or sometimes clumping. These are species reference dimensions, not measurements of the collection specimen.

milestones.text: Purchased at Carlsons' Greenhouse in a 4-inch pot.
milestones.title: Joined the collection

milestones.text: Close photographs showed large tubercles, dark-tipped spines, tiny cream flowers or buds, and a red club-shaped fruit.
milestones.title: Identification observations

nameStory.text: Linnaeus published Cactus mammillaris in 1753; Kew dates the present Mammillaria combination to 1886.
